new_statements.quote: Na południu Śląska w gwarze jabłonkowskiej występuje akcent inicjalny – na pierwszej sylabie wyrazu, jest to wyraźny wpływ języków grupy czesko-słowackiej. Na pozostałym obszarze Śląska Cieszyńskiego ten typ akcentu występuje obocznie z typowym dla polszczyzny akcentem padającym na przedostatnią sylabę w wyrazie. Na pozostałym obszarze śląskim, podobnie jak w języku literackim, panuje akcent paroksytoniczny.
new_statements.translation: In the south of Silesia, in the Jabłonków subdialect, initial stress occurs – on the first syllable of the word; this is a clear influence of the languages of the Czech-Slovak group. In the rest of Cieszyn Silesia this type of stress occurs side by side with the stress typical of Polish, falling on the penultimate syllable of the word. In the remaining Silesian area, as in the literary language, paroxytonic [penultimate] stress prevails.
new_statements.citation: Winiarska, Izabela. [c. 2010]. "Charakterystyka dialektu śląskiego", in Halina Karaś (ed.), Gwary polskie. Przewodnik multimedialny (online; ISBN 978-83-62844-10-4), section "Cechy językowe dialektu śląskiego", paragraph on akcent. Corroborated first-hand by Malinowski 1873: 31 (§ 71) for the Opole dialect and Bystroń 1885: 29-30 (§ 64) for the Cieszyn/Lachian dialect.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable throughout the Silesian area, as in standard Polish. Malinowski 1873: 31 adds that in the Opole dialect this holds without exception ('stets'), even in -ija nouns (lelija, marija) where standard Polish has antepenultimate stress; Bystroń 1885: 29 says the same for the Cieszyn (Lachian) dialect ('zwykle na głoskę przedostatnią').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Jabłonków (Jablunkov) subdialect in the far south: initial stress (Czech/Slovak influence); elsewhere in Cieszyn Silesia initial stress alternates with penultimate (Winiarska). Bystroń 1885: 29-30: stress wavers in -ija/-yja loans (biblija, Maryja); Czech-borrowed 'poxvalen' stressed on 2nd or 3rd from end; fused phrases (svęntyjan, svatydux) take one penultimate stress; the question 'a vidźiś?' always has final stress and questions generally shift stress to the final vowel (pitch about a fifth higher). Nikel 1908: 12 notes stress on the -i- of loans in -ia/-io/-ium.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress; dialect descriptions of spoken varieties (Opole, Upper Silesian industrial district, Cieszyn/Zaolzie). The Winiarska page is a synthesizing dialect characterization in a multimedia dialectology guide, not a fieldwork monograph; the primary statements from Malinowski 1873 and Bystroń 1885 are 19th-century.
new_statements.identity_note: sile1253 = Silesian (szl), the Silesian dialect group of Lechitic. The deciding statement (Winiarska) covers the whole 'dialekt śląski' and singles out the Jabłonków (Jablunkov, CZ) subdialect with initial stress and the rest of Cieszyn Silesia with variable initial/penultimate stress. The corroborating primaries are sub-dialect specific: Malinowski 1873 = Opole (Oppeln) dialect, northern Silesia; Bystroń 1885 = 'gwara laska' of the Stonawka and Łucyna basins in Teschen Silesia (today Czech Zaolzie; a Cieszyn Silesian variety); Nikel 1908 = Upper Silesian industrial district (Zabrze/Bytom/Katowice). I did not extract Glottolog dialect codes for these subvarieties (the page's tree JSON failed to parse).

sources.note: Penultimate (paroxytonic) stress over the whole Silesian area as in standard Polish; exception: initial stress in the Jabłonków subdialect in the far south (Czech-Slovak influence), and in the rest of Cieszyn Silesia initial stress alternates with penultimate. sources.citation: Bystroń, Jan. 1885. O mowie polskiej w dorzeczu Stonawki i Łucyny w Księstwie Cieszyńskim. Kraków: Drukarnia Uniwersytetu Jagiellońskiego (offprint from Rozprawy Wydziału Filologicznego Akademii Umiejętności, vol. 12). § 64 "Akcent", pp. 29-30.
sources.note: p. 29, § 64: "W gwarze laskiéj pada akcent, jak w języku ogólnym, zwykle na głoskę przedostatnią." (In the Lachian [Cieszyn/Teschen] subdialect stress falls, as in the general language, usually on the penultimate syllable.) Notes wavering stress in -ija/-yja loans (biblija, Maryja), penultimate stress on fused phrases (svęntyjan), final stress in the question 'a vidźiś?' and generally rising final stress in questions; p. 30: "Akcent w gwarze laskiej jest więc wyraźnie polski" and even the Silesian and NE-Moravian dialects further west have Polish stress. sources.citation: Malinowski, Lucian [Lucjan]. 1873. Beiträge zur slavischen Dialectologie. I. Ueber die Oppelnsche Mundart in Oberschlesien (1. Heft: Laut- und Formenlehre). Inaugural-Dissertation, Universität Leipzig. Leipzig: Bär & Hermann. § 71 "Accent", p. 31.
sources.note: p. 31, § 71: "Wie im g. p. so fällt auch im opp. der accent stets auf die vorletzte silbe, sogar in den subst. fem. auf -ijâ, z. b. lelija, g. p. lilija, marijân, g. p. màri-ja." — stress always penultimate in the Opole (Oppeln) dialect as in standard Polish, even in -ija nouns where standard Polish has antepenult. Primary fieldwork description of the northern (Opole) Silesian dialect. fetched sources from Polona (public domain).

sources.note: Part I (vowels and consonants only; Part II never appeared) has no accent section (no 'Betonung/Akzent' anywhere). One incidental remark, p. 12, § 16: "In den Lehnwörtern auf urspr. io, ion, ia, ium hat i stets den Ton und wird diphthongisch — ii̯ gesprochen, z. B. nacii̯a..., penzii̯ŏ (Pension), vilii̯ŏ (Vigil), familii̯a..." — i.e. the -i- (penultimate syllable) always bears the stress in such loans. fetched sources from archive.org.
